introduction_markdown: Time allowed: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions. Section I is designed to be answered in 1 hour and Section II in 1 1/2 hours; you are advised to divide your time accordingly. In Section II answer EITHER a, b and c OR d, e and f of each question. For your guidance the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation of your answers. In calculations you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Where necessary, assume: the acceleration due to gravity on the surface of the earth, $g = 10\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$; the speed of light in air, $c = 3.0\times10^{8}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; the charge on an electron, $e = 1.6\times10^{-19}\,\mathrm{C}$. Calculators are allowed.

figures.legende: Uniform plank of length 2 m resting on a support A at its midpoint; a 60 N weight hangs at the left end, an 80 N weight hangs at a distance x to the right of the support; the reaction R of the support points upwards.

incertitudes: Le sujet n'imprime pas de total par question : les totaux (`points` de l'exercice) sont la somme des points imprimés bloc par bloc (Section I : 6+4+8+6+9+7 = 40 ; Section II : 20 par question, soit 100 au total).

Les schémas, diagrammes et graphes demandés à l'élève (tracé de graphe, diagramme de rayons, champ électrique ou magnétique, tension d'entrée et de sortie, schéma de montage) ne sont pas produits comme figures du corrigé : ils sont décrits dans le corrigé (axes, points clés, forme).

Figure 2 : le poids de 60 N est lu à l'extrémité gauche de la planche, donc à 1 m du support A (planche de 2 m, appui en son milieu) ; x est la distance du poids de 80 N au support. Ces lectures sont celles du schéma imprimé.
Question 4 : la planche a une masse négligeable, donc son poids n'intervient ni dans l'équilibre des moments ni dans la valeur de R.

questions.enonce_markdown: State two conditions necessary for the system to be in equilibrium. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
1. The **resultant force is zero**: the sum of the forces in one direction equals the sum of the forces in the opposite direction (here, upward force = total downward force).
2. The **resultant moment is zero**: the sum of the clockwise moments about any point equals the sum of the anticlockwise moments about the same point (principle of moments).

questions.enonce_markdown: Calculate the distance, $x$, of the $80\,\mathrm{N}$ object from the support when the system is in equilibrium. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Take moments about the support A. The $60\,\mathrm{N}$ weight is at the end of the plank, $\dfrac{2}{2} = 1\,\mathrm{m}$ from A (anticlockwise). The $80\,\mathrm{N}$ weight is at a distance $x$ from A (clockwise). The reaction R passes through A and has no moment about A.

At equilibrium: clockwise moment = anticlockwise moment

$80 \times x = 60 \times 1$

$x = \dfrac{60}{80} = 0.75\,\mathrm{m}$

**$x = 0.75\,\mathrm{m}$ (75 cm).**

questions.enonce_markdown: Calculate the force, $R$, on the plank by the support. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The plank is in equilibrium, so the upward force equals the total downward force:

$R = 60 + 80 = 140\,\mathrm{N}$

**$R = 140\,\mathrm{N}$** (the plank has negligible weight).
